# parity-fuzz --mode atflag baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode atflag --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# MALFORMED DELIMITER-FLAGS (fixed in subst.rs): the mode now emits bare,
# with-name `${(j)a}` / `${(s)a}` / `${(_)a}` (delimiter flag, no delimiter) and
# `${(j:x)a}` / `${(_:x:)a}` (bad/non-empty arg) inside a `{ … } 2>&1` group.
# C jumps to `flagerr` (c:subst.c:2505/2527 → "error in flags near position N")
# for these; the port wrongly emitted "bad substitution" for `j`/`s`/`_`. The
# `{ … } 2>&1` wrap is required because the error fires at EXPANSION time before
# `print` runs, so a bare `print … 2>&1` would not capture it. Reverting the fix
# yields 39 divergences on seed 1. The empty-name form `${(j)}` is deliberately
# NOT generated — it diverges on a separate (paren-stripping) path. Bug #1015.
#
# FIXED (no longer gaps): the RANGE (`[lo,hi]`) subscript on an EMPTY array
# now pads correctly via getarrvalue's `nular` port (c:params.c:2570-2585),
# so `${#${(@)a[1,2]}}` is 1 for `a=()`; and the `(A)` array-force flag now
# collapses a lone empty-string result to an empty array
# (`${#${(A@)a[1,2]}}` is 0).
#
# One remaining known-gap class: a SEARCH subscript (`[(R)pat]`) on an EMPTY
# array, observed through a length count. zsh returns a nular (a single
# empty element) so `${#${(@)a[(R)*]}}` is 1 for `a=()`, where the port
# returns 0. Unlike the range case (which flows through getarrvalue), the
# search-subscript arm returns a SCALAR "" from the value-search path; making
# it array-shaped nular requires seeding isarr/split_parts through that
# scalar path — cross-cutting plumbing for a pathological case (a reverse
# search of an EMPTY array, visible only via `${#}`). The bare/quoted splat
# already matches (one empty word). Left as a known gap.
a=(); print -rl -- "${#${(@)${(@)a[(R)*]}}}"
a=(); print -rl -- "${#${(@)a[(R)*]}}"
a=(); print -rl -- "${#${(@o)a[(R)*]}}"
a=(); print -rl -- "${#${(o@)a[(R)*]}}"
